recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-900 and CDJ-2000. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't reliably recognised by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, XDJ-AZ, OPUS-QUAD, OMNIS-DUO, PRIME 4+ and SC LIVE 4.

pioneer_only.headline: Expected to work on all selected equipment

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-900 and CDJ-2000. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't reliably recognised by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, XDJ-AZ, OPUS-QUAD and OMNIS-DUO.

FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't reliably recognised by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, XDJ-AZ, OPUS-QUAD, OMNIS-DUO, PRIME 4+ and SC LIVE 4.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-900 and CDJ-2000. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't reliably recognised by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, XDJ-AZ, OPUS-QUAD, OMNIS-DUO, PRIME 4+ and SC LIVE 4.
